# Pets

Pepper, cat, present throughout.

Pepper doesn't have much of a plot of her own — she's the constant against which everything else in Jordan's life gets measured. Right now she's doing what she always does: claiming the green rug, waiting by the door, and reading Jordan's moods with more accuracy than Jordan usually credits himself with.

The green rug arrived August 1st and Pepper claimed it immediately with the slow territorial roll cats do. It's become her fixed spot — she was on it the night before the lease renewal (9/14) and again two days later (9/16), "same spot, same curl," as Jordan put it, treating her constancy almost as a comfort against a week full of moving parts (a new manager, an onsite interview, a portfolio deck).

The clearest pattern in these entries is that Pepper shows up hardest exactly when Jordan is struggling. When the design review with Marcus went badly (8/3), she curled against his leg and later slept on his chest — something Jordan noted she "only does when I'm down," and something he takes as evidence she knows. When the restructuring news got worse and Jordan shut down for the afternoon (8/24), she climbed into his lap and purred hard enough to vibrate his sternum; he sat with her for an hour "just existing." After the bad sleep from the recurring office dream (8/14), she was staring at him from the foot of the bed when he woke at 4am. She's a fixture of the bad nights as much as the good ones.

She also has comic, unbothered moments that don't carry any weight beyond themselves: sitting on forbidden counters during phone calls with Mom (8/7, 8/9), knocking a water glass off the nightstand at 2am and watching Jordan clean it up like he was the unreasonable one (8/1), batting at his shoelaces after a run (8/19), meeting him at the door out of hunger rather than sentiment though Jordan chose to read it as moral support anyway (9/16). During Jordan's open-mic practice for "Fast Car," she sat on the amp and howled along during the quiet verse, which made him laugh hard enough to lose the chord progression (8/17). During Dev's session testing the Coda app, she left the room at the loud slapped bass notes and came back only once they'd stopped, which Jordan read as her having "made her position clear" (9/3).

The one notable expansion of her role: Mom's Labor Day visit (9/6). Pepper usually hides from guests, but she slept on Mom's lap for an hour — the kind of detail Jordan flagged without much comment, though it sits next to the visit where he also finally told his mother about the work situation he'd been sitting on since July.

Nothing about Pepper is in question or motion right now — no vet visits, no aging concerns, no logistics tied to the possible job change or the lease. She's simply there, on the rug, at the door, on the pillow (she'd claimed it before Jordan could on 9/9, so he took the other one, "as is our arrangement"), watching the window on 9/15 "like she's expecting someone" when, per Jordan, it was just the Tuesday bird. The open thread, if there is one, is entirely external to her: if Northlight comes through and changes Jordan's living situation or commute, what happens to the arrangement he's built his days around — the one where she's always exactly where he left her.
